$meta.name: Local Operator mobile design tokens
$meta.what: The source of truth for the native Local Operator mobile app's visual system: colour roles for both themes, the mobile type ramp, space, radii, touch targets, safe-area rules, elevation and motion.

derivedFrom.contribution: the accent and semantic triples, the line weights, the radii cap, the two shadows, the motion durations and easings, the contrast floors, and the warm-paper register the whole system is written in

the two brand palettes — localOperatorDark and localOperatorLight — which are the ROLES this file ships: canvas, surface, elevated, sunken, messageSurface, rowHover, rowSelected, the four ink weights, hairline, borderControl, the accent ramp, accentAlt, and the info role the site has no equivalent for
the role names themselves; this file keeps them so a palette can be swapped between the desktop app, the phone web client and this app without a translation layer
the phone-shaped decisions: the 16px input floor for iOS focus-zoom, the touch-target floors, the machine-voice/sans split, and the mobile type ramp's register

$meta.themeContract: Every colour token is either { light, dark, role } (theme-varying) or { value, role } (theme-invariant). A reader resolves a theme with `t.value ?? t[theme]`. Nothing here is DTCG: this file is consumed by design/tokens/contrast-contract.mjs and read by hand, and the `role` strings are the reason it is worth reading.
$meta.hexCase: lowercase; hex case is not significant
$meta.ratioMethod: WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula on sRGB hex, rounded to 2dp
$meta.checkedBy: design/tokens/contrast-contract.mjs — `node design/tokens/contrast-contract.mjs` recomputes every permitted foreground x ground pair and every component triple in both themes and exits non-zero on a violation. Run it after editing any colour in this file.
$meta.shipped: design/tokens/tailwind-preset.js exposes these roles as Tailwind utilities so the app can be built with either NativeWind or Uniwind; docs/design/brand-kit.md is the prose that explains the choices and docs/design/components.md is the primitive spec.
$meta.notStable: This is a 0.1.0 researched draft. The palette VALUES are the shipped brand and should not be retuned; the mobile-specific SCALES (type, touch, safe-area) are proposals that the first implementation pass is expected to validate on a real device.

color.$note: Roles, never hues. A component names bg-surface or text-ink-muted and the theme decides what that is. The three grounds (canvas -> surface -> elevated) are the desktop app's own ramp, because the phone is the same product on a smaller screen and a user who has seen the desktop app should recognise the surface. Values marked with a `ratio` note carry a measurement taken from this file on 2026-09-29 with contrast-contract.mjs.

canvas.role: page ground; the transcript's own paper

surface.role: cards, list rows, inputs, panels that sit in the flow

elevated.role: sheets, dialogs, popovers, hovered and pressed rows

sunken.role: inset wells: tool output, diffs, code, tracks

message-surface.role: the user turn's own fill. Distinct from `surface` because a turn is not a panel — see docs/design/brand-kit.md § 3

row-hover.role: an interactive row under the finger. A step of the panel's own hue, never a tint of the accent

row-selected.role: the row you are in. Ranked above hover by lightness AND chroma, so the two are distinguishable without colour vision

ink.role: headings, prose, answers, the transcript's body

ink-muted.role: secondary prose, tool-row verbs, count chips, panel headers

ink-disabled.role: disabled control text only; exempt under WCAG SC 1.4.3 as an inactive control

hairline.role: decorative 1px rule, panel separator. NEVER the sole boundary of anything you can press or type into (measured 1.25:1 light / 1.46:1 dark on canvas)

hairline-strong.role: a hovered or focused rule where a hairline would vanish; the frame edge. Still decorative

border-control.role: structural: the border of every control and any 1px rule that is the sole boundary of required content. Measured 3.42:1 light / 3.93:1 dark on canvas, 3.65 / 3.58 on surface, 3.92 / 3.30 on elevated — it clears the 3:1 non-text floor on all six grounds in both themes

accent.role: the one primary action, links, the focus ring, the streaming caret, the active indicator

accent-hover.role: hover and the in-a-well accent step

accent-active.role: pressed fill; and the ink on accent-muted in light

accent-wash.role: the faintest tint: the approval card's ground, a selected row's wash, an accent-tinted callout

accent-muted.role: the solid tinted fill: badge and chip backgrounds, the selected segmented item

accent-border.role: the 1px edge on a tinted chip or a selected card. Measured 4.33:1 light / 3.56:1 dark on canvas

on-accent.role: ink on the accent fill. Measured 5.33:1 (light) and 8.58:1 (dark). White on the dark accent is 2.16:1 and is prohibited outright

accent-alt.role: the second identity colour: subagent and peer-session marks, so a delegated turn is not drawn in the primary action's colour

accent-alt-wash.role: accent-alt's faintest tint, for a peer or subagent row's ground

success.role: done, passed, +N diff counts, the running-agent glyph

success-wash.role: success ground; the diff-add line tint

success-border.role: the structural edge of a success callout

warning.role: blocked, held, degraded, a pending decision that is not a failure

warning-border.role: the structural edge of a warning callout

danger.role: failed, stopped, −N diff counts, the attention pulse, destructive actions

danger-wash.role: danger ground; the diff-remove line tint

danger-border.role: the structural edge of a danger callout and of the stop control

info.role: neutral system notes, a queued tool call, diff hunk headers

info-border.role: the structural edge of an info callout

diff.$note: The diff is not a decoration: it is the evidence a change happened. Ink comes from the semantic ramp; the LINE TINT is the semantic wash, which keeps a long diff readable without turning the well into a colour field.
diff.$tintLadder: The three row tints are NOT the same values as the semantic washes in dark, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic. A wash is painted on `canvas`; a diff tint is painted inside the `sunken` well, which is darker than the canvas. Reusing the dark wash there (#16281d) measured 1.11:1 against the well — a step no reader can see, so the diff's only channel was its text colour. The dark tints are re-solved to a perceivable step (1.28-1.32:1 against `sunken`) while keeping chroma: add #23352a, remove #432a26, hunk #22303f. The LIGHT tints are unchanged at 1.04-1.07:1, because at high L* the hue difference is what the eye reads, where at L* 10 chroma compresses and only a luminance step survives. Both facts are asserted by design/tokens/contrast-contract.mjs § 'diff tint ladder'.
diff.$measuredInk: Ink on its own tint, light / dark: success 4.86 (on #e6f1ea) / 6.14 (on #23352a), danger 4.94 / 5.02, info 4.86 / 6.24 — all above the 4.5:1 text floor.

diff-add.role: an added line's text, and the +N counter

diff-remove.role: a removed line's text, and the −N counter

diff-context.role: an unchanged context line inside a diff: dimmer than the change, so the change is what the eye lands on

fixed.$note: Literal values the system commits to, theme-invariant by construction, exposed under these exact names.

scrim.role: the sheet/dialog scrim. A literal warm-black at 70% rather than a per-theme value, because a scrim's job is to recede the content behind it and that job does not change with the theme

shadow-color.role: the base for both elevation shadows

focus-ring-photo-inner.role: inner stroke of the two-tone ring over a photograph (a sent image, a poster)

focus-ring-photo-outer.role: outer stroke of the same ring

type.$note: The register is the desktop app's, not the site's: a tool has no hero, so the largest routine step is a page title. This ramp is the shipped phone web client's ramp with the body steps raised one step for a device held at arm's length. `size` is the authored number in points (iOS pt) and scale-independent pixels (Android sp) — the same number, because both platforms' default text sizes agree at these steps. `lineHeight` is a unitless multiplier, `weight` is a variable-axis position, and `face` names which family the step pairs with (a step never encodes a family).

display.use: the screen title: Sessions, a session's conversation name on its own screen

title.use: section and sheet titles, the model sheet's heading

heading.use: group headings, card titles, list section headers

body-lg.use: the transcript's assistant prose and the user's own turn. The reading surface: one step above `body` because it is read for minutes at a time

body.use: default prose, form labels, the composer's text. 16 is also the floor at which iOS does not zoom on focus — see § 5 of the brand kit

body-sm.use: list rows, secondary panels, a tool row's summary, card body

meta.use: captions, counts, the attention word, a subagent's model and effort

label.use: button labels, tab labels, segmented items

mono.use: the machine voice: paths, model slugs, ids, elapsed times, counts

mono-sm.use: the same voice in a dense row: tool names, diff counts, the cwd line

mono-code.use: code blocks and diff lines. The one place mono is allowed to wrap

mono-label.use: uppercase badge and status text, a version string

sans.why: open apertures and a tall x-height, which is what makes 14px row copy legible; also quiet next to a serif

mono.why: the machine-voice signal: a filename set in mono is evidence, a filename set in the body face is a claim

display.why: NOT shipped in the app's UI. Reserved for the store listing, the onboarding's first frame and the launch screen, where the register is 'a well-made thing' rather than 'a tool'. See docs/design/brand-kit.md § 4

numeric.$note: Tabular numerals on anything that sits in a column or changes in place: elapsed times, counts, diff totals, todos 0/3. A proportional numeral in a column that ticks makes the row jitter.

dynamicType.$note: iOS Dynamic Type and Android font scaling both scale these steps automatically and that is wanted: a reader who has asked their phone for larger text has asked this app too. The rules below are the ones a naive implementation gets wrong.
dynamicType.scaling: left ON for every text style in the app. No `allowFontScaling={false}` anywhere in the tree; on Android, no size set in `dp` where it should be `sp`.
dynamicType.fixedGeometryRule: A 1.4 cap is permitted only where the row's height is pinned by something other than its text AND the text can ellipsize (a session row's title, a tool row's name, a chip label). Capping a step whose text has room to grow is a defect: the cap is a layout constraint, never a preference.
dynamicType.survivalFloor: Every layout must survive 1.3x with no clipped or overlapping content. Test at 1.3x, not 2.0x, as the routine case; 2.0x is the accessibility case and it is acceptable for a long value to wrap to a second line there, never for it to be cut.
dynamicType.avoidFixedHeights: Rows are sized by content plus padding, not by a fixed height. Where a minimum is enforced (44pt touch targets) it is a MIN and the row grows past it.

space.$note: A 4pt base with three tiers, as the desktop app's branding doc groups it. Consistency of tier matters more than the exact value: mixed tiers are what make a layout look unconsidered.
space.note-on-max-width: The desktop kit's four fixed container widths do not port: a phone and tablet are resizable and often split. What ports is the reading measure — a transcript column stays between 45 and 75 characters however wide the screen is.

radius.$note: The kit's ramp, assigned by what the object IS rather than what looks good on it in isolation. Nothing above 16 exists; an out-of-scale value renders a square corner rather than silently working.

assignment.xs: the progress track, the scrollbar thumb, a selection checkbox
assignment.sm: a control: button, input, textarea, segmented item, badge, chip, tool row, skeleton bar
assignment.md: a panel or card read as one block: list card, inline alert, the approval card, a sheet's inner section
assignment.frame: the composer, and the composer alone
assignment.full: the status dot, the send/stop button, an avatar

size.$note: Touch geometry. Two floors, and they are floors rather than targets: iOS HIG asks 44pt, Material asks 48dp, and the shipped phone web client already uses min-h-11 (44px) for its Button and Chip — which is why the app's default control height is 44 and not the desktop's 38.

slop.$note: A small visual control may stay visually small when its hit area is padded out to 44. The hit area may never overlap another control's, and it is measured from the control's own frame, not from an icon inside it.

icon.$note: lucide, one stroke weight, and the weight is never written down: lucide's own default of 2 draws one pen at every size on its 24px grid. Sizes below are the slots; an icon inside a control agrees with that control.
icon.strokeWidth: library default (2) — never restated, never overridden
icon.stateGlyphs: The transcript does not use lucide for tool state: the shipped client's ✓ ✗ ⟳ ⋯ – ☐ ☑ are text glyphs in the mono face, chosen because they survive every system font and never become tofu. Keep them as text; an icon font would be a second pen.

safeArea.$note: The rules that keep content out from under a notch, a Dynamic Island, a home indicator, a rounded corner and an Android gesture bar. `env(safe-area-inset-*)` on the web is the same number as RN's `useSafeAreaInsets()`; both must be applied, and a hardcoded inset is a defect.

rules.top: the header's top padding = inset.top; the header is otherwise 56pt tall
rules.bottom: the composer's bottom padding = max(inset.bottom, 8) — a composer flush to the home indicator is unreachable at the bottom of the screen
rules.left: inset.left in landscape only; a phone with a notch rotates its inset to the left edge

keyboard.avoidance: The composer rides the keyboard. On iOS the transcript's scroll offset adjusts so the last entry stays visible; on Android `windowSoftInputMode=adjustResize` with edge-to-edge disabled for the transcript.
keyboard.columnVsViewport: The composer's cap is a fraction of the SCROLL COLUMN, not of the viewport — the two diverge the moment a keyboard opens, which is when the mistake bites. The shipped client learned this at 360x780 where a 60dvh card put its send button under the column's clipped foot.

landscape.insets: left and right are non-zero on a notched phone; content must not sit under the island in landscape
landscape.maxWidth: the transcript column caps at 620pt and centres, rather than stretching a 45-character measure across a 900pt-wide landscape screen

tablet.columns: list + detail side by side above 700pt of width; the detail column caps at 640 and the list at 360
tablet.splitscreen: every layout is measured at one half of a split (about 320pt) as well as at full width; a two-column layout that does not collapse is a defect

elevation.$note: There are exactly two shadows, and they are the kit's. Elevation for in-flow content is a BACKGROUND STEP (canvas -> surface -> elevated), never a shadow: a phone has less room for a soft edge and more need for the grounds to be told apart by their own value. `androidElevation` is the Material equivalent for the two cases that need one; RN maps `shadow*` (iOS) and `elevation` (Android) separately and both must be set or one platform gets nothing.

overlay.role: a sheet, a dialog, a popover: an object that LEAVES the flow

frame.role: an image or capture shown as a matted object rather than inline

elevation.androidSurfaceTint: not used: the tint would come from the palette's accent and repaint a panel the ground ramp already distinguishes

motion.$note: The kit's durations and easings, plus the native translation of each. No spring, no bounce, no overshoot anywhere: nothing in this interface is an object with mass. Every animated thing is information appearing or a state changing.

durationUse.instant: colour-only micro-feedback: a press tint on a row
durationUse.fast: hover, focus, border and colour transitions; the scrim fade
durationUse.base: an indicator moving between two positions: the streaming caret, a segmented selection sliding
durationUse.slow: a sheet or a dialog entering; a height change
durationUse.reveal: content entering after a load, used once per screen and never in a list
durationUse.draw: an SVG stroke drawing in — the launch animation only
durationUse.close: the closing gesture of a multi-step sequence
durationUse.beat: one beat of a multi-step emphasis sequence, roughly the pace of reading one short line

shimmer.role: the streaming sweep across a session name or the working line's label. The only loop on the reading surface

spinner.role: the roster's loading ring and a running tool's glyph — the ring only, never the glyph: a text glyph that rotates stops being a glyph

pulse.role: the attention dot on a row waiting for a decision. The ONE motion reserved for danger; do not spend it on ordinary work

loadbar.role: the thin accent segment sweeping the top of the transcript while older history loads

native.$note: What each token is in the two native animation systems, so the same curve is used on both sides of the bridge.
native.reanimated: withTiming(value, { duration: <ms>, easing: Easing.bezier(a, b, c, d) }) — the four cubic-bezier control values above map one-to-one to Easing.bezier
native.coreAnimated: Animated.timing(value, { toValue, duration, easing: Easing.bezier(...), useNativeDriver: true })
native.forbidden: withSpring, Animated.spring, Easing.elastic, Easing.bounce, any overshoot or damping-ratio parameter. Spring makes the duration non-deterministic, and a duration that cannot be reasoned about cannot be budgeted for a reduced-motion reader

budget.why: under WCAG SC 2.2.2's five-second threshold, above which a pause control becomes mandatory

reducedMotion.$note: Reduced motion is not a kill switch: functional feedback survives. Ask of every animation not 'can this be removed' but 'what does it TELL the reader, and how do they learn it with the animation off'.
reducedMotion.detect: iOS: AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled() and the reduceMotionChanged event. Android: AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled() (Android's 'Remove animations' developer setting and the system animation scale) — plus a data-saver/low-power signal, resolved into the SAME flag so 'should this move' is one decision in one place
reducedMotion.floor: a global transition cap: durations clamp to 120ms and looping animations stop at their resting frame. Cap rather than zero: an instantaneous colour change loses the affordance that a press IS feedback

mustSurvive.streaming: the shimmer stops; the row keeps a still accent caret and the working line keeps its elapsed seconds and verb, so 'in progress' is still legible
mustSurvive.attention: the danger pulse stops; the word 'approval' and the static dot remain, which is the channel that carried the meaning anyway
mustSurvive.loading: the spinner stops; a static ellipsis in the mono face plus a polite live region replaces it
mustSurvive.sheet: the sheet appears without a rise; the scrim still separates it
mustSurvive.skeleton: the pulse stops; the bars keep their resting tone, which is lifted above the ground precisely so a still frame still reads as a placeholder

z.$note: Six levels, named. A seventh is a sign something is stacked that should be route-level.

focus.$note: One ring for the whole system, defined once, never per component. On a phone this is rarely seen, but a hardware keyboard, a switch control and a TV-style remote all reach it — and the shipped client keeps it for exactly that reason.

twoTonePhotoRing.role: a control over an arbitrary photograph — a sent image, a poster — where the ground's luminance is unknown

focus.formOffsetWhy: a field's own 1px border sits exactly where a 2px offset would put the ring, and the two strokes read as two borders rather than one focused control

contrastFloors.$note: Applies to every foreground the system ships except ink-disabled, which is exempt under SC 1.4.3 as an inactive control's text, and a disabled control's boundary, exempt under SC 1.4.11 for the same reason.
